rationale:
Evidence from iteration 2 (ki 0.5): the score was 51.3691 against 51.3695 for iteration 1 (ki 0.0). Max_error was unchanged at 0.0609 (oval), 0.0648 (s-bend) and 0.0622 (slalom), and line-loss events stayed at 0, 1 and 1. The integral term therefore had no measurable effect, so the steady-bias hypothesis is rejected. Per the Evaluator's rule (2), the error is probably a start transient or an early overshoot. It sits just past the 0.06 m off-track limit on every track, and across iterations 0 to 2 it stayed in a 0.061 to 0.065 band whatever base_speed, kp, kd or ki were set to. Progress of 0.12 to 0.15 shows the robot leaves the line early in each run. Changing kp and speed did not move the error, which points to the start of the run or the first bend.

Change: controller.kd from 0.2 to 0.4, with ki kept at 0.5 and every other field held at iteration 2 values. This is the Evaluator's recommended next test. More derivative action should damp a fast early swing if the swing is driven by the rate of change of the signal. I expect max_error to fall slightly, perhaps to about 0.055 to 0.06 on some tracks. I do not expect completion yet, because base_speed 1.2 gives an average speed well below the 1.5 m/s needed to finish in 3.0 s.

Hypotheses: (a) the early swing is a rate-driven overshoot, so higher kd reduces max_error; (b) if max_error is still near 0.061 on all tracks, the cause is a fixed initial lateral offset or the start condition, and the next test should widen the sensor footprint (sensor_size 0.016) or move the sensors further forward (y 0.07) to give earlier steering lead; (c) if kd 0.4 causes jitter, steering_oscillation will rise above about 0.15. Note that the off-track limit is effectively fixed at 0.06 m, since body_width 0.18 gives only 0.0575, so the error has to be reduced rather than the limit widened.

Next measurements: max_error, progress, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation per track, plus the distance travelled before the first off-track event if available.
